question: After Californian towns banned thin carry-out bags, how much of the plastic saved was cancelled by extra bin-bag purchases?
answer: About 30%. Using shop scanner data, Taylor found the bans cut carry-out bag plastic by about 18,000 tonnes a year, while bin-bag purchases rose by about 5,400 tonnes, offsetting about 29%. Sales of the smallest bin bags jumped 120%. The free shopping bag had been doing a second job under the kitchen sink.
move: Ask what second job the banned thing was quietly doing.
ask: What useful job was the thing I just cut quietly doing?
trap: Treating the old bags as used once, then thrown straight away.
source: Taylor, J. Environmental Economics and Management, 2019
reference: Taylor, Bag leakage: The effect of disposable carryout bag regulations on unregulated bags, Journal of Environmental Economics and Management, 2019
